A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LapSum research. Their complete 18-page documents, including equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–D, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original LapSum classification, permutation-learning, sensitivity and computational-efficiency results, alongside baseline results attributed to earlier work.

after.justification: v2 retains original LapSum experiments and reports revised accuracies, computational measurements and expanded alpha sensitivity results.

M1.justification: The underlying Laplace-CDF construction, inverse-based operators, losses and model architectures remain unchanged. Trainable alpha already appears in v1. The added parallelization discussion and Appendix C.4 explain computation of operations already claimed in v1 rather than establishing a redesigned method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CIFAR-100, ImageNet-1K, ImageNet-21K-P, MNIST/CIFAR-10 nearest-neighbor classification and Large-MNIST permutation learning. The CPU/GPU scaling scenarios are retained; expanded alpha sweeps change settings within existing coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within Tables 1–4 and the computational comparisons. This includes the classification sorting baselines, nearest-neighbor variants, permutation baselines, and Bitonic, NeuralSort, Splitter Selection, optimal transport and Sander variants in the scaling plots.

E3.justification: Figures 6 and 8 expand the plotted alpha range from approximately -1.5 through -0.1 to -5000 through -0.1 and explicitly compare frozen versus trainable alpha. The stated models, budgets and hyperparameters in Tables 5–6 remain unchanged; the larger sweep is not reconciled with Appendix D's retained narrow grid.

E4.justification: The alpha sensitivity analysis now tests frozen versus trainable alpha across a substantially broader range for CIFAR-100 and ImageNet-1K. Both training distributions remain represented after consolidating the panels. Numerical-error, scaling and training-trajectory analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v1's sensitivity plots explicitly identify minimum–maximum ranges, means and medians with standard deviations. The replacement plots retain bars and bands but no longer define those summaries. Table 2's 10 and 2 seeds and the critical-difference testing approach are unchanged; no increase in runs is established.

E6.justification: Results are substantially revised across classification, permutation learning, sensitivity and computational comparisons. Table 1's LapSum top-5-training ACC@1/ACC@5 changes from 57.20/86.84 to 58.07/87.50; its uniform-distribution row changes from 63.22/87.10 to 64.53/88.51. Table 4's n=15 result changes from 31.6 (82.6) to 33.9 (82.4). Table 2's ImageNet-1K ACC@1 values and Figures 10–13 also change. The expanded sensitivity results involve different settings, while Table 3 remains unchanged.

T1.justification: New Appendix C.4 derives derivatives for multiple inverse-function outputs and presents an O(L+n) recurrence argument, substantially extending the mathematical treatment. v2 also corrects the spurious one-half term in Theorem 3.2's proof and revises Theorem 4.1's complexity reasoning. Some revised formulas introduce inconsistent indices, notably in Proposition 4.2 and Appendix B.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction newly emphasize efficient parallelization as a contribution. The principal claims concerning unified differentiable ordering, closed-form computation, complexity and high-dimensional performance remain.

C2.justification: Section 5.1 removes the interpretation that LapSum needs no predetermined selection of m leading scores and excels at any dimension. The broader interpretations of scalability, accuracy and adaptive alpha behavior remain; no substantial limitations discussion is added.

D1.justification: v1's promise of a future GitHub release becomes a specific full-code repository pointer in v2. Section 4.1 additionally identifies prefix scans for parallel computation. Pseudocode notation is revised, but Algorithm 1 retains a k=n branch after its interval index changes to j, reducing implementation clarity.

R1.justification: The cited-work set remains unchanged; reference changes mainly supply bibliographic metadata. However, removing the explicit contrast with Petersen et al.'s predetermined m-score selection narrows one claimed advantage over prior work.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and narrative remain intact. Changes primarily comprise local copyediting, expanded ranking explanations, attempted normalization of w/k notation and function arguments, and affiliation and reference metadata updates. Appendix C gains subsection C.4.

P2.justification: v1's Figure 5 moves into the introduction as v2's Figure 2. Figures 6 and 8 are redesigned to distinguish frozen/trainable alpha, consolidating CIFAR-100 panels into Figure 6 and retaining ImageNet in Figure 8. Computational plots and table sizing are reformatted, while the overall two-column design remains.

improvement.justification: The corrected ranking proof, additional derivative analysis, broader alpha comparisons and concrete code pointer provide useful improvements. However, v2 introduces index inconsistencies in Proposition 4.2, Appendix B and Algorithm 1, while removing explicit uncertainty definitions from the sensitivity plots. These affect mathematical clarity and reproducibility. The PDFs establish meaningful benefits and regressions without a reliably assessable net direction; higher reported scores alone do not resolve that tradeoff.
